summary: Specialized housing refers to residential buildings that serve vulnerable populations such as seniors, individuals with disabilities, or those requiring supportive care, by combining bed-sitting rooms or dwelling rooms with conventional dwelling units under one roof. These integrated housing types are critical to addressing gaps in Toronto's housing continuum, providing residents with both independence and access to on-site services and supports that traditional residential buildings are not designed to offer. At its October 30, 2025 meeting, Planning and Housing Committee adopted Item 2025.PH25.17, directing staff to conduct a comprehensive review of Type G loading space requirements for mid-rise developments. Type G loading requires buildings to fully internalize a truck's ability to maneuver, collect waste, and swing up a waste bin without reversing onto a public road, resulting in high ground floor ceilings and significant loss of ground floor area. The adopted item asks staff to examine the 31-unit threshold that triggers these requirements, consult with industry stakeholders, conduct jurisdictional analysis of global best practices, and report back by the second quarter of 2026 on innovative solutions including smaller trucks, turntables, on-street collection, and alternative waste storage. This motion seeks to extend that review to explicitly capture specialized housing…
decided: City Council on March 25 and 26, 2026, adopted the following: 1. City Council request the Chief Planner and Executive Director, City Planning, the Executive Director, Development Review, and the General Manager, Solid Waste Management Services, to review the applicability of Type G loading space requirements for specialized housing projects that include combinations of bed‑sitting rooms/dwelling rooms and dwelling units, as part of the October 30, 2025 Planning and Housing Committee Item 2025.PH25.17 – Type G Loading Requirements and Waste Management for Mid‑Rise Developments motion amendment.
